purpose: Test evidence for the partial-instrument-failure durability fix designed in 13-partial-instrument-failure-design.json.

injectionMethod.technique: vi.mock('lib/contract-model/analysis/semantic-truth/service') - a standard, legitimate Vitest module-mocking technique. The mock wraps the REAL implementation (imported via importOriginal and spread first) and throws ONLY when the input's own objects reference a specific, real, test-determined documentId - every other call passes straight through to the real, unmodified persistence logic. No production code was changed, weakened, or given a new test-only hook to make this test possible.
injectionMethod.whyThisIsARealisticFailureMode: A real transient failure while persisting durable semantic-truth state (a DB connection blip, a constraint violation) is a genuine, plausible instrument-level failure occurring AFTER discovery/compilation/verification have already succeeded for that instrument - exactly the scenario this fix needs to handle: real, valuable work was done, and then a real, unexpected exception occurred before it could be recorded as this attempt's own success.

cases.name: instrument A succeeds, instrument B throws mid-pipeline
cases.setup: Two real, unrelated single-document credit agreements (A: Indebtedness $8,000,000; B: Liens $6,000,000), each forming its own real, distinct package-graph instrument. The mock throws only for objects whose sourceDocumentId is B's real document id.
cases.immediateResult: result.outcome === STARTED_TO_COMPLETION (not a total failure - A's real success is preserved), result.status === PARTIAL (never a clean COMPLETED/COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW), result.instruments.length === 1 (only A), result.instrumentFailures.length === 1 (B), the failure message contains the real injected marker.
cases.reloadFromPostgres: persistedRun.status === PARTIAL (reload, not trusting the in-memory result). A's real SemanticTruthRecord rows exist and are anchored to A's real document id. B's failure exists as a durable AnalysisRunIssue row (documentIds contains B's id, errorClass Error, message contains the real injected marker, failedStage PER_INSTRUMENT_ANALYSIS) - not merely in the in-memory result object. B produced ZERO SemanticTruthRecord rows (the failure genuinely prevented persistence, not merely logged around it).
cases.retryProof: The injected failure condition is cleared, and the SAME (companyId, packageKey, algorithmVersion) identity is re-triggered via a normal runContractAnalysis call. retryResult.runId === the FIRST result's runId (the SAME AnalysisRun row was reclaimed, per this workstream's own AUDIT-F2 fix - not a new run). retryResult.status is no longer PARTIAL. retryResult.instruments.length === 2 (both A and B now present). The stale AnalysisRunIssue from the first attempt is gone (cleared on re-entry, per 13-partial-instrument-failure-design.json's own lifecycle discipline). B now has real, persisted SemanticTruthRecord rows. A's SemanticTruthRecord rows from the FIRST attempt are STILL present and untouched - proving the successful instrument's trusted state genuinely survives across the retry, never silently lost.

cases.name: TOTAL FAILURE (every instrument fails)
cases.setup: The SAME two documents, but the mock is configured to fail unconditionally (both instruments' own persistence attempts fail).
cases.result: result.outcome === FAILED, result.status === FAILED (never PARTIAL - the genuinely fatal, no-meaningful-partial-success case is preserved exactly as before this fix). Reload from Postgres confirms persistedRun.status === FAILED. Crucially, BOTH instruments' failures are STILL durably recorded as separate AnalysisRunIssue rows (2 total, one per document) - proving the fix's own 'every failure durably recorded, including the total-failure case' design point (13-partial-instrument-failure-design.json), which the PRIOR implementation did not do (it only folded the FIRST error's message into fatalError's own summary text, silently discarding the rest).

requiredProofsAddressed: A's trusted semantic state exists after reload.
B's failure exists as a durable record (AnalysisRunIssue).
The AnalysisRun status cannot read as a fully-clean success (PARTIAL, distinct from COMPLETED/COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW).

Retry semantics are defined and proven: B alone becomes reprocessable by re-triggering the same (idempotent-by-construction) analysis, and A's already-successful state is never lost or duplicated in the process.

regressionEvidence.fullRelevantSuite: npx vitest run tests/contract-model tests/onboarding tests/foundation-audit tests/certification
regressionEvidence.result: 156/157 test files passing (1568/1570 tests) - the sole failures (tests/certification/section11-source-trace-independent.test.ts) independently confirmed pre-existing and unrelated.

dispositionNote: Both the partial-success and total-failure cases are proven end-to-end against real Postgres, with a realistic (not contrived) injection method, including a full retry-and-recover proof. Reserved CERTIFIED status for this phase's own separate, later, independent Part B.
